in_sanskrit.name: पुलक
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The name Pulak is derived from the Sanskrit word 'pul', which means 'red'. The name can be translated to English as 'red one' or 'red-skinned'. In Hindu mythology, Pulak is a name given to several characters. One of them is the son of the demon king Ravana from the epic Ramayana. He is also known as Indrajit, and is a powerful asura (demon) who is an expert in magic and warfare.

in_hindi.long_meaning: The Hindi name Pulak is derived from the Sanskrit word 'pul', which means 'red'. The name can be translated to Hindi as 'लाला' (lalaa), which means 'red'.
